content: 1. Armodafinil Interaction: Armodafinil reduces the plasma levels and therapeutic effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. Dose adjustments or alternative therapies should be considered to maintain efficacy. 2. Velpatasvir as a CYP Substrate: Velpatasvir is metabolized by CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4 enzymes. Drugs that are moderate-to-potent inducers of these enzymes can significantly lower velpatasvir plasma concentrations, potentially reducing its therapeutic effect. Close monitoring or alternative treatments are recommended. 3. Aspirin/Citric Acid/Sodium Bicarbonate Interaction: These agents increase gastric pH, which reduces the solubility and absorption of velpatasvir (practically insoluble at pH > 5). This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Separate administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir and antacids by at least 4 hours to minimize this effect. 4. Atazanavir Interaction: Atazanavir increases the plasma levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary to avoid potential toxicity. 5. Atorvastatin Interaction: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases atorvastatin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1 transporters. This interaction may increase the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Monitor closely and adjust atorvastatin dosage as needed. 6. Betrixaban Interaction: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases betrixaban levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally daily. Monitor for bleeding risks. 7. Bosentan Interaction: Bosentan decreases the plasma levels and efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. 8. Calcium Carbonate Interaction: Calcium carbonate increases gastric pH, reducing velpatasvir solubility and absorption. Separate administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir and calcium carbonate by at least 4 hours to mitigate this effect. 9. Carbamazepine Interaction: Carbamazepine significantly reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 and P-gp transporters. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 10. Chloramphenicol Interaction: Chloramphenicol increases the plasma levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 11. Cimetidine Interaction: Cimetidine increases gastric pH, reducing velpatasvir solubility and absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Administer H2 receptor antagonists either simultaneously with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir or 12 hours apart, ensuring the dose does not exceed famotidine 40 mg twice daily. 12. Clarithromycin Interaction: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects. 13. Clobazam Interaction: Clobazam reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. 14. Colchicine Interaction: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases colchicine levels by inhibiting P-gp transporters. Avoid colchicine use with P-gp inhibitors, especially in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If coadministration is necessary, reduce colchicine dosage or frequency as per prescribing guidelines. 15. Conivaptan Interaction: Conivaptan increases the plasma levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 16. Cyclophosphamide Interaction: Cyclophosphamide increases the plasma levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 17. Dabrafenib Interaction: Dabrafenib reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 18. Dexamethasone Interaction: Dexamethasone reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. 19. Dexlansoprazole Interaction: Dexlansoprazole increases gastric pH, reducing velpatasvir solubility and absorption. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. If medically necessary, administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with food 4 hours before omeprazole 20 mg. The use of other PPIs has not been studied. 20. Digoxin Interaction: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases digoxin levels by inhibiting P-gp transporters. Monitor digoxin levels closely and adjust the dose as needed, following prescribing guidelines for digoxin concentration increases of <50%.
